posts.note: Critique of the Black et al. 2014 quetiapine-in-BPD trial; past analysis only, plus one own-event date.
Short musing on the Seroquel name; only an own-event date.
Review of Seroquel FDA adverse-event data and bipolar depression efficacy; only newsletter-output statements are forward-looking.
Satire recasting UnitedHealth Group executive stock sales as Mordor, Inc. insider trading; one joke call flagged insincere, plus a summit announcement.
Humorous self-audit against the Hippocratic oath; newsletter paywall policy, event reminder, one joke.
Both statements are quoted third parties (DomainTools researcher, UHG CEO Witty).
Anonymous TheLayoff.com poem reproduced by the author; the one forecast belongs to the poem.
Review of the Tarleton 2017 magnesium crossover trial; only event announcements are forward-looking.
Recruitment notice for Fermata and Acacia clinical trials (present tense) plus event announcements.
Essay on attention, social media, reading and declining sex rates; two vague societal calls.
Essay on physician self-disclosure and stigma; SAINT launch is reported as a same-day event, not a forecast.

statements.quote: It’s also a live-action series of conferences called “Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment”—the next is in NYC on May 5th.
statements.context: Opening boilerplate of a post dissecting the Black et al. 2014 quetiapine trial in borderline personality disorder. The author says his own conference series, Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT), holds its next event in New York City on May 5th (2024).
statements.note: Event announcement for the author's own conference; scheduling claim, control candidate.

statements.quote: I am hosting a live event. It’s May 5th.
statements.context: Closing of a short post on the origin of the name Seroquel. The author announces that he hosts the live Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 NYC event on May 5th (2024).
statements.note: Event announcement, own conference; control candidate.

statements.quote: Please consider subscribing to this newsletter, and becoming a paid subscriber, it requires a lot of work to do, and I am likely to do more of them if you subscribe!
statements.context: Closing subscription pitch of the Seroquel bipolar depression review. The author says he is likely to write more comprehensive pieces like this one if readers subscribe.
statements.note: Conditional statement about the author's own newsletter output; control candidate.

statements.quote: The above discourse probably warrants a dedicated article, so I’m going to give it a rest, for the time being.
statements.context: Footnote 4 of the Seroquel bipolar depression post, attached to the discussion of D2 receptor occupancy and extrapyramidal side effects. The author says the topic deserves its own future article and that he sets it aside for now.
statements.note: Weak statement of intent about future newsletter content; control candidate.

statements.quote: We await answers, before these executives flee to the Grey Havens, in which Sauron-controlled hedge fund “GreyHome Partners LLC” recently announced an $83m investment.
statements.context: Satirical post that recasts the reported $101.5m-$105m of UnitedHealth Group executive stock sales made before the DOJ antitrust probe became public as insider trading by Sauron and the board of Mordor, Inc. The author quips that the executives will flee before answers arrive.
statements.note: Satire; the fleeing-to-the-Grey-Havens line is a joke, not a real expectation. The sincere content of the post is past reporting, not a forecast.

statements.quote: Updates: Join me as I proudly co-chair the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction, taking place May 15-16 at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach and live-streamed online.
statements.context: Closing announcement of the insider trading satire post. The author says he will co-chair the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction on May 15-16 (2024) at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach, also live-streamed online.
entities: Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction
Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach
statements.note: Event announcement of the author's own appearance; scheduling claim.

statements.quote: The discovery in the subsequent legal matters is getting more streamlined, at least.
statements.context: Short post on RansomHub leaking Change Healthcare data, including PHI and contracts between Change/UHC and counterparties. The author remarks, sardonically, that there will be subsequent legal matters over the breach and that the leaked contracts will make discovery in them easier.
statements.note: Sarcastic aside; presupposes future litigation over the Change Healthcare breach.

statements.quote: Some new posts will have a paywall, and most will not, but 202 articles were jailbroken yesterday for all of the internet to enjoy.
statements.context: Housekeeping note at the top of the Hippocratic oath post. The author says he removed the paywall from 202 backlog articles and that, from now on, some new posts will be paywalled but most will not.
statements.note: Own newsletter paywall policy; control candidate.

statements.quote: Quick Reminder: Upcoming May 5th Event: Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment ., NYC. Tickets. Get Them.
statements.context: Reminder line in the Hippocratic oath post for the author's Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment live event in NYC on May 5th (2024).
statements.note: Event announcement, own conference; control candidate.

statements.quote: Numerous contracts are going to be called into question. This part is… an issue.
statements.context: Humorous self-audit against the Hippocratic oath clause that a physician teaches the art to pupils 'but to none else'. The author jokes that his public newsletter (571 articles) violates this, so numerous contracts will be called into question.
statements.note: Joke; no real expectation that contracts will be challenged.

statements.quote: Indeed, if this data and more becomes fully leaked, it could be devastating to the individuals affected.
statements.context: Post on RansomHub selling Change Healthcare data on the dark web. Block quote from Sean McNee, PhD (DomainTools) via SC Media, which the author presents as evidence that the nightmare scenario has begun. Conditional: a full leak could devastate the affected individuals.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Sean McNee); the author frames it approvingly but does not restate it in his own words.

statements.quote: We're going to bring it back much stronger than it was before.
statements.context: Same post. Quote from the UnitedHealth Group CEO (Mr. Witty) on the April 16 earnings call, via a Motley Fool transcript, about restoring Change Healthcare after the cyberattack. The author quotes it right after noting Witty's $89m share sales and does not endorse it.
statements.note: Quoted third party (UHG CEO Witty); the author does not adopt it and implies skepticism.

statements.quote: The revenues are so much that not even a massive cyber attack matters financially to UHC.
statements.context: Post asking why UnitedHealth Group executives sold $105m in shares before the DOJ probe was revealed. Amid discussion of unreported Optum layoffs (WARN Act) and a share price up 12.3% on the week, the author asserts that UHC's revenues are so large that the Change Healthcare cyberattack will not matter to it financially.
statements.note: Present-tense assertion with a forward reading about the financial impact of the cyberattack on UHG.

statements.quote: what if the DOJ probe wasn’t why the executives dumped shares? Maybe there is another, worse reason?
statements.context: Closing thesis of the same post. After reviewing the $101.5m in executive stock sales between Oct. 16 and Feb. 26, the author speculates that a worse, still-unknown reason for the sales exists at UnitedHealth Group.
statements.note: Phrased as questions; speculation that a hidden, worse problem at UHG exists and may surface. Borderline.

statements.quote: according to Optum insiders sharing information with The Frontier Psychiatrists , comments on TikTok, and The Layoff.com, the Optum Virtual Care team is being shut down.
statements.context: Post contrasting UnitedHealth Group's 2022 praise of virtual care (34 million telehealth visits in 2020) with reports that Optum Virtual Care is being shut down. The author relays insider, TikTok and TheLayoff.com reports, calls them as yet unconfirmed, and treats the shutdown as a remarkable about-face.
statements.note: Relays unconfirmed reports; repeated as 'Except now they are, per unconfirmed reports, not.' The title asks whether Optum virtual care is over.

statements.quote: We will, I suppose, have to wait and see. I’m sure they have something that will generate significant shareholder value planned.
statements.context: Closing of the Optum Virtual Care post. After asking where in-person capacity for 34 million extra visits a year will come from, the author says, sarcastically, that UnitedHealth Group/Optum surely has a plan that will generate significant shareholder value.
statements.note: Sarcastic tone; the underlying expectation is that UHG acts to raise shareholder value. Vague.

statements.quote: We'll wait a few months for the ire to fade. And that's when the new round of "affected" will be made.
statements.context: Post reproducing an anonymous poem left on TheLayoff.com about Optum/UnitedHealth Group layoffs after the Change Healthcare breach. The poem's closing lines predict another round of layoffs ('affected' employees) after a few months. The author only calls it a good-enough poem.
statements.note: Third-party poem (possibly AI-written, per the author); the author does not explicitly adopt the prediction.

statements.quote: 1. May 5th, 6-9 PM is Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment NYC LIVE . Get Those Tickets!
statements.context: Programming note in the magnesium post: the author's Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment live event in NYC on May 5th, 6-9 PM (2024).
statements.note: Event announcement, own conference; control candidate.

statements.quote: May 7th at ATA Nexus in Phoenix!
statements.context: 'Other Times to Catch Me Live' list at the end of the magnesium post. The author says he will appear at ATA Nexus in Phoenix on May 7th (2024).
statements.note: Event appearance announcement; scheduling claim.

statements.quote: Join me as I proudly co-chair the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction , taking place May 15-16 at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach and live-streamed online.
statements.context: Same list. The author will co-chair the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction on May 15-16 (2024) at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach, also live-streamed.
entities: Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction
Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach

statements.quote: And then…A Virtual, on June 5-7th! Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently
statements.context: Same list. The author points to a virtual conference on June 5-7th (2024), 'Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently' (affiliate link).
entities: Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently
statements.note: Event announcement with an affiliate link; listed under times to catch the author live.

statements.quote: Today: a psychedelic compound, well on its way to becoming a medicine.
statements.context: Opening of Ibogaine I, a review of Cherian et al. 2024 (Nature Medicine) on magnesium-ibogaine therapy (MISTIC) in special operations veterans with traumatic brain injury. The author asserts that ibogaine is well on its way to becoming a medicine.
statements.note: Implies future approval or medicalization of ibogaine; no date given.

statements.quote: It's worth noting that this is an extremely hard study to do, and it will be extremely hard to blind, if impossible.
statements.context: Near the end of Ibogaine I. Looking past the open-label Cherian et al. study toward controlled trials of ibogaine, the author predicts that blinding such trials will be extremely hard or impossible.
statements.confidence_phrase: will be extremely hard to blind, if impossible
statements.note: Methodological forecast about future ibogaine trials.

statements.quote: so we may need to look at design that look at within subjects controls, because of the challenge of doing a blind control trial comparing between subjects, and not within subjects.
statements.context: Same passage. The author says future ibogaine trials may need within-subject control designs instead of blinded between-subject trials, because participants cannot be kept unaware of a life-changing experience.
statements.note: Hedged; part design recommendation, part prediction about how ibogaine trials will be designed.

statements.quote: Next, I’m Appearing at… May 7th — ATA Nexus in Phoenix!
statements.context: Upcoming events list in the post announcing clinical trials for depression at Fermata (NYC) and Acacia Clinics (Sunnyvale). The author says he will appear at ATA Nexus in Phoenix on May 7th (2024).
statements.note: Event appearance announcement; repeats the magnesium post.

statements.quote: May 15-16, Miami Beach + Virtual— I’m the Co-Chair!
statements.context: Same list. The author will co-chair the May 15-16 (2024) Miami Beach summit (the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction), also offered virtually.
entities: Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction
statements.note: Event appearance announcement; repeats the insider trading and magnesium posts.

statements.quote: And then…A Virtual Conference, June 5-7th: Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently
statements.context: Same list. Virtual conference on June 5-7th (2024), 'Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently' (affiliate link).
entities: Neurodiversity: A Conference for and About Doctors Who Think Differently
statements.note: Event announcement with an affiliate link; repeats the magnesium post.

statements.quote: I am not sure if writing has the staying power of 15-second videos.
statements.context: Essay on attention, social media and declining reading. After noting over a million TikTok views in one week versus about 80k newsletter reads a month, the author doubts that written media will keep its staying power against short video.
statements.note: Expressed doubt, not a firm call; echoed by 'I wonder if books have staying power'.

statements.quote: When sex has gone out of fashion, we have a problem for the future of humanity.
statements.context: Same essay. Citing the drop in teens reporting ever having had sex (from over half three decades ago to 30% in 2021), the author says the decline is a problem for the future of humanity.
statements.note: Vague societal claim; hard to resolve.

statements.quote: If too many of us are out and about, publicly speaking about our experience, together, it becomes less plausible to punish any individual for the temerity to live our lives with dignity.
statements.context: Post on self-disclosure of psychiatric illness by physicians, prompted by the Carlat Report podcast episode that anonymized its participants. Conditional claim: if many clinicians disclose publicly, punishing any individual becomes less plausible.
statements.note: Conditional social-dynamics claim about stigma; hard to resolve.
